quests.question: ___ that the market was shrinking, the company opened five new stores.
quests.hint: This formal phrase signals a concession — a fact that doesn't change the outcome — in official writing.
quests.explanation: 'Notwithstanding that' introduces a formal concession — despite the shrinking market, the company still expanded.

quests.question: The rebrand worked ___ customer surveys showed a clear improvement in trust.
quests.hint: This formal phrase sets a specific limit on how far the rebrand's success extends.
quests.explanation: 'To the extent that' means the same as 'insofar as' — success is measured specifically by improved trust scores.

quests.question: Raw material costs kept rising, ___ the company raised prices twice in one year.
quests.hint: Rising costs directly led to a pricing decision.
quests.explanation: 'So' introduces a result — rising costs caused the repeated price increases.

quests.question: ___ the merger to fall through, thousands of jobs would be at risk.
quests.hint: The verb form given after the blank determines which word grammatically fits — check carefully.
quests.explanation: 'Were' inverts a hypothetical condition without 'if' — 'were the merger to fall through' matches 'would be at risk'.

quests.question: The old factory ran on a single shift, ___ the new one operates around the clock.
quests.hint: Two factories are being placed side by side in contrast.
quests.explanation: 'While' can contrast two related facts — two facilities with two different schedules.

quests.question: The union rejected the offer ___ it fell short of the agreed minimum increase.
quests.hint: A specific shortfall explains the rejection.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the direct reason for a decision — falling short of the minimum caused the rejection.

quests.question: ___ compelling was the evidence that the committee reversed its earlier decision.
quests.hint: This word pairs with an adjective and can trigger inverted word order when placed first.
quests.explanation: 'So' combines with an adjective to trigger inversion when fronted — 'so compelling was the evidence' reverses the normal word order.

quests.question: The simulation is accurate ___ it accounts for atmospheric pressure at sea level.
quests.hint: This formal phrase sets a specific limit on how far the simulation's accuracy extends.
quests.explanation: 'Insofar as' means 'to the extent that' — the accuracy depends specifically on this one factor.

quests.question: The mission was delayed ___ engineers detected a fault during the final inspection.
quests.hint: A specific discovery explains the delay.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the direct reason for a delay — the detected fault caused the postponement.

quests.question: ___ that funding was limited, the observatory completed the survey on schedule.
quests.hint: Common in official documents, this phrase concedes a point without changing the outcome.
quests.explanation: 'Notwithstanding that' introduces a formal concession — despite limited funding, the survey finished on time.

quests.question: Ground-based telescopes are affected by atmospheric distortion, ___ space telescopes avoid it entirely.
quests.hint: Two types of telescopes are being formally contrasted.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' formally contrasts two related facts — two telescope types with two different limitations.

quests.question: ___ did the probe survive the landing, but it also began transmitting data within minutes.
quests.hint: Fronting this phrase triggers inverted word order — the subject and helper verb swap places.
quests.explanation: 'Not only' is the only option here that requires inverted word order when placed at the start of a sentence.

quests.question: ___ the source requested anonymity, the reporter withheld the person's name.
quests.hint: An accepted fact is the basis for an editorial choice.
quests.explanation: 'Given that' introduces an accepted fact as the basis for a decision — the request for anonymity justified withholding the name.

quests.question: The coverage was balanced ___ both sides were given equal space to respond.
quests.hint: This formal phrase sets a specific limit on how far the balance claim holds.
quests.explanation: 'To the extent that' means the same as 'insofar as' — the balance is measured specifically by equal space given to both sides.

quests.question: The headline was attention-grabbing, ___ it didn't accurately reflect the article's content.
quests.hint: An eye-catching detail didn't match the substance underneath.
quests.explanation: 'But' introduces a contrast — a catchy headline didn't match the actual content.

quests.question: ___ the editor caught the error sooner, the correction would have run before print.
quests.hint: Look closely at the verb form right after the blank — only one of these four options matches it.
quests.explanation: 'Had' inverts a past hypothetical condition without 'if' — 'had caught' matches 'would have run' in the same past-hypothetical tense.

quests.question: Print editions run a single correction column, ___ online articles can be corrected instantly.
quests.hint: Two publishing formats are being placed side by side in contrast.
quests.explanation: 'While' can contrast two related facts — two formats with two different correction processes.

quests.question: The retraction was issued ___ the original claim couldn't be independently verified.
quests.hint: A verification problem explains the retraction.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the direct reason for a decision — the unverifiable claim caused the retraction.

quests.question: ___ that the odds were against them, the underdog team reached the final.
quests.hint: This legal-sounding phrase works like 'although', but fits formal or official writing best.
quests.explanation: 'Notwithstanding that' introduces a formal concession — despite poor odds, the team still reached the final.

quests.question: ___ harder the opponent pushed, ___ more determined the team became.
quests.hint: Two comparative ideas increase together in this fixed pattern.
quests.explanation: 'The...the' shows that one increase causes a matching increase — more pressure led to more determination.

quests.question: The first half was cautious and defensive, ___ the second half was fast and attacking.
quests.hint: Two halves of the same match are being formally contrasted.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' formally contrasts two related facts — two very different styles of play.

quests.question: The training program helps ___ it addresses the specific skills gap identified in the survey.
quests.hint: This formal phrase sets a specific limit on how far the program's benefit extends.
quests.explanation: 'Insofar as' means 'to the extent that' — the benefit is limited to addressing this specific gap.

quests.question: ___ the pilot region reported strong results, the initiative will expand nationwide next year.
quests.hint: An accepted fact is the basis for an expansion decision.
quests.explanation: 'Given that' introduces an accepted fact as the basis for a decision — strong pilot results justify the expansion.

quests.question: Critics predicted the policy would fail within months, ___ it remains in place five years later.
quests.hint: A confident prediction still didn't come true.
quests.explanation: 'Yet' shows surprising contrast — a predicted failure never actually happened.

quests.question: ___ does the new terminal handle twice the passenger volume, but it also cut average wait times in half.
quests.hint: This phrase demands inverted word order right after it, unlike the other three options.
quests.explanation: Starting a sentence with 'not only' triggers subject-verb inversion, a pattern the other options don't share.

quests.question: The redesign succeeded ___ complaints dropped by more than half within a year.
quests.hint: This formal phrase sets a specific limit on how far the redesign's success extends.
quests.explanation: 'To the extent that' means the same as 'insofar as' — success is measured specifically by the drop in complaints.

quests.question: The proposal passed easily ___ months of consultation had already addressed most objections.
quests.hint: Prior preparation explains the smooth outcome.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the direct reason for a result — earlier consultation caused the easy approval.

quests.question: ___ any delegate object to the proposal, the vote will be postponed until further discussion.
quests.hint: Check the verb form that follows the blank; it grammatically rules out three of the four options.
quests.explanation: 'Should' inverts a possible future condition without 'if' — 'should any delegate object' matches the base verb form given here.

quests.question: The initial framework addressed only large corporations, ___ the revised version also covers small businesses.
quests.hint: Two versions of the same framework are being placed side by side in contrast.
quests.explanation: 'While' can contrast two related facts — two versions with two different levels of coverage.

quests.question: ___ that the committee faced fierce opposition, the final policy passed with a clear majority.
quests.hint: In formal writing, this phrase concedes a fact while the main outcome still stands.
quests.explanation: 'Notwithstanding that' introduces a formal concession — despite fierce opposition, the policy still passed comfortably.
